answers.answer: `SchedulerCore.start()` calls `_plan_all_routes()` before reconciliation. That method builds its request from every `self.plan.tasks` entry, carrying dependencies and other task facts, so blocked dependents are included. The later `_assign()` path filters to tasks whose state is READY and which have no resource conflict; whole-plan routing and READY assignment have different scopes.

The bridge is `DecisionAssignmentPort.plan()`, which delegates to `plan_full_dag()`. That function checks the batch task bound, builds a `DecisionRequest` for each task, then calls `batch_decisions.persist()` once with the full tuple. The batch planner jointly matches routes for the bounded request set; it is not one independent M2 decision operation per task.

The scheduler persists each task’s `route_metadata`, `route_status`, and `route_reason`, including `unavailable` when metadata is empty, and sets `routing_complete` after recording the map. `RunState.to_dict()` includes these fields; the SQLite repository stores the serialized state document. On restart, `_plan_all_routes()` returns when `routing_complete` is true, preventing a repeat. A failed or invalid map does not set that flag, so a later start can retry.

Whole-plan mapping produces advisory route metadata; the `PlannedRoute` contract says it is non-reserving. The actual reservation occurs when `_assign()` submits a READY-task assignment to `claim()`, which calls `reservation.claim()`. That transaction checks capacity and task/resource eligibility, records the assigned route, and writes a start intent to the outbox. The initial map itself does not launch work.

READY assignment performs a new quota preflight and builds fresh candidates at a timestamp derived from that refresh; when a supported provider’s profile is unavailable in the refresh, its candidate quota status is changed to `unknown`. The new batch result supplies the assignment metadata, which `reservation.claim()` stores as `assigned`; the earlier planned metadata is not blindly copied into the assignment.

`refresh()` turns poll errors, malformed or stale observations, and missing observations into explicit unavailable status and reason facts; antigravity refresh exceptions also fail closed. If refresh raises at the routing or READY-assignment boundary, callers substitute an unavailable `quota_refresh_failed` fact. `quota_aware_requested_at()` uses the maximum of the request time, current time, and valid finite `observed_at` values, tying decision candidates to the post-refresh observation time.

`test_ready_revalidation_uses_changed_quota_and_m1_owns_the_only_reservation` first maps a route under one quota snapshot, starts the Scheduler, changes the quota before `step()`, and asserts that the READY assignment refreshes quota and selects `codex-luis`; it also asserts one claimed task and one attempt. Separately, `test_full_dag_is_recorded_then_ready_route_is_revalidated_without_executor` asserts that the initial map includes a blocked dependent, while READY assignment uses different route metadata, leaves the dependent’s recommendation intact, and creates only a pending outbox item with no execution port. These are source assertions; tests were not run.

unknowns: The snapshot does not establish live account quota, provider availability, or runtime behavior beyond the source assertions cited.
